mentions.context: on individuals.171 This is exactly the opposite view to what we have in Pico’s thesis and it might just be the same case as in thesis 8, where, as we have seen, Pico critically reacts to Ockham through the mediation of Thomas. Thesis 36 states that two accidents which differ only in number are not placed in the same subject.172 Let us have a look at Thomas’s commentary on the Sentences, 2, d. 13, q. 1, a. 3, argument 2. Thomas claims there that things which are mutually united and separated while remaining the same in number

non tamen pro se sed pro omnibus particularibus; nam hoc commune ‘homo’ non potest ridere.
